################################################################################################
### Posteam Avg
################################################################################################

### Posteam Avg Function
```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Example date to filter by (replace with your actual value)
# x <- as.Date("2024-09-07")  # This should be a date in the format "YYYY-MM-DD"

# Initialize empty data frames
data.last20 <- data.frame()

posteam20 <- function(season_in, week_in) {
  # Rolling 14-game averages by TEAM, as-of the start of (season_in, week_in)
  data.last20 <- data %>%
    dplyr::filter(season < season_in | (season == season_in & week < week_in)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(posteam, dplyr::desc(season), dplyr::desc(week), dplyr::desc(game_date)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(posteam) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 14) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  data_means <- data.last20 %>%
    dplyr::group_by(posteam) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
                     .groups = "drop")

  # Rename columns to include "posteam_avg_" prefix (except for join keys)
  colnames(data_means) <- ifelse(colnames(data_means) == "posteam",
                                 "posteam",
                                 paste0("posteam_avg_", colnames(data_means)))

  # Add join keys for week-based merge
  data_means$season <- season_in
  data_means$week   <- week_in

  return(data_means)
}


```


```{r}
# posteam20(season_in = 2025, week_in = 18)
```


```{r}
# Get unique season/week pairs present in the dataset (plus a placeholder next-week per season)
unique_season_weeks <- data %>%
  dplyr::distinct(season, week) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(season), dplyr::desc(week))

next_weeks <- data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(season) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(week = max(week, na.rm = TRUE) + 1L, .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(week), week >= 1L, week <= 22L)

unique_season_weeks <- dplyr::bind_rows(unique_season_weeks, next_weeks) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(season, week) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(season), dplyr::desc(week))
```


### Loop Posteam Avg
```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Initialize an empty data frame to store results
data.last20.avg.off <- data.frame()

# Loop through season/week pairs and apply the function (week-based cutoffs; no within-week drift)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(unique_season_weeks))) {
  s <- unique_season_weeks$season[i]
  w <- unique_season_weeks$week[i]

  temp_result <- posteam20(s, w)

  # Append to the final dataset
  data.last20.avg.off <- dplyr::bind_rows(data.last20.avg.off, temp_result)
}

# View the final merged dataset
# print(data.last20.avg.off)

```


# Merge Data with Posteam averages (week-based)
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

merged_data <- data %>%
  dplyr::left_join(data.last20.avg.off, by = c("posteam", "season", "week"))

print(merged_data)
```

  data_means <- data.last20 %>%
    dplyr::group_by(defteam) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
                     .groups = "drop")

  # Rename columns to include "defteam_avg_" prefix (except for join keys)
  colnames(data_means) <- ifelse(colnames(data_means) == "defteam",
                                 "defteam",
                                 paste0("defteam_avg_", colnames(data_means)))

  # Add join keys for week-based merge
  data_means$season <- season_in
  data_means$week   <- week_in

  return(data_means)
}

##############################################################################
### League Avg
##############################################################################

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Example date to filter by (replace with your actual value)
#x <- as.Date("2024-09-07")  # This should be a date in the format "YYYY-MM-DD"

# Initialize empty data frames
data.last640 <- data.frame()

league_avg <- function(season_in, week_in) {
  # League-wide "baseline" averages as-of the start of (season_in, week_in).
  # We build a 32-team x 14-game panel (last 14 games per team), then average across that panel.

  data.last640 <- data %>%
    dplyr::filter(season < season_in | (season == season_in & week < week_in)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(posteam, dplyr::desc(season), dplyr::desc(week), dplyr::desc(game_date)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(posteam) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 14) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  data_means <- data.last640 %>%
    dplyr::summarize(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
                     .groups = "drop")

  # Add join keys
  data_means$season <- season_in
  data_means$week   <- week_in

  # Prefix non-key columns
  colnames(data_means) <- ifelse(colnames(data_means) %in% c("season", "week"),
                                 colnames(data_means),
                                 paste0("NFL_avg_", colnames(data_means)))

  return(data_means)
}


```



```{r}
# league_avg(season_in = 2025, week_in = 18)
```




### Loop League Avg
```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Re-use unique_season_weeks created earlier (season/week pairs, incl. placeholder next week)

# Initialize an empty data frame to store results
data.last20.avg.league <- data.frame()

# Loop through season/week pairs and apply the function (week-based cutoffs)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(unique_season_weeks))) {
  s <- unique_season_weeks$season[i]
  w <- unique_season_weeks$week[i]

  temp_result <- league_avg(s, w)

  # Append to the final dataset
  data.last20.avg.league <- dplyr::bind_rows(data.last20.avg.league, temp_result)
}

# View the final merged dataset
# print(data.last20.avg.off)

```


```{r}
# Fix NaN at first game of a season

# Replace NaN with the column mean
reference_rows <- !is.na(data.last20.avg.league$season) & data.last20.avg.league$season < 2026
stopifnot(any(reference_rows))
data.last20.avg.league <- data.frame(lapply(data.last20.avg.league, function(x) {
  if(is.numeric(x)) {
    replacement <- mean(x[reference_rows], na.rm = TRUE)
    if (is.finite(replacement)) x[is.nan(x)] <- replacement
  }
  return(x)
}))

```



# Merge Data with League averages (week-based)
```{r}

merged_data <- merged_data %>%
  dplyr::left_join(data.last20.avg.league, by = c("season", "week"))

print(merged_data)
```
